title: Customer evidence & usable proof
summary: Named public stories cluster in vacation-rental and multi-market hospitality operators, with one boutique-hotel valuation write-up and no hotel-group body in this pack. Figures are Conduit-attributed, sometimes internally inconsistent on dates and automation denominators, and should be used one named story at a time with the printed caveat.
markdown:
# Customer evidence & usable proof

This library uses **named case-study pages only**. The stories index also says Conduit is trusted by hundreds of organizations and by 300+ hospitality brands in 120+ countries; that is a company reach claim, not named product-adoption evidence, and logo or industry-link walls are not treated as proof. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers)

Pages were retrieved 19–20 September 2026. “Using Conduit since” dates are printed as-is. Results are attributed to Conduit’s write-ups, not independently verified. Stories usually name the platform as a whole ([AI Agents](#knowledge/product-agents), [Inbox](#knowledge/product-inbox), [Workflows](#knowledge/product-workflows)) rather than a SKU; an integration name is not evidence of a supported action.

## Proof by customer and buying situation

### Vacation-rental and property-management operators

| Customer | Operating / buying situation | Named use | Reported result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Haven Vacation Rentals | Smokies STRs; Conduit since Feb 2024; installed earlier at ~40% automation with few workflows | Workflows, knowledge-base teaching, guest messaging | 90% automation across ~270 properties; support need from ~25 people to two per shift; 14 January listings with no extra support hires; scores held 4.8–4.9 |
| Cascadia Getaways | Oregon vacation rentals; first PM acquisition; page says using since Dec 2024 and deployed in March | Guest comms, knowledge base, routine AI answers | 60% automation and 4.9 communication score across 100 properties; 150 properties per support rep on shift |
| HomeHop | Cleveland/Akron STRs; failed prior AI vendor; Google Voice lockout; using since June 2025 (page also says ~two years) | Email, SMS, OTA, voice AI 1–7 AM, SuiteOP workflows | ~40→108 listings without extra guest-support hires; 70% automation; overnight coverage in those hours |
| Canbnb | Canberra STR manager; 7→170 properties; 630-message backlog | Inbox; Hostaway/WhatsApp/email/SMS/chat; guest/owner/vendor inboxes | ~1,500 messages/week, 60% handled by AI; index headline 150% growth |
| Bocobay | High-end PM, Aruba and Curaçao; left Intercom (June 2024) | Unified email, WhatsApp, phone, live chat; notes/tags | Page: 80% resolution rate, “100s” hours saved; body does not show the math |
| Cosmica | Italy + Dubai; using Sep 2025 Dubai / Oct 2025 Italy | Messaging plus arrival, maintenance, cleaning workflows and Dubai upsells | No extra support team; outsourced VAs eliminated; upsells/cross-sells ~5% of Dubai revenue at peak |
| Bali Luxury Stays / Easy BnB | Exit-oriented PM; 14 VAs; using since Dec 2024 (founded 2025 on the same page) | Guest-messaging AI; night 100% / day up to 85% | ~$22k/month labor savings; 11 VAs replaced; 75 units, 0 extra FTE; ~80–85% messaging automation |
| The Flex (Flex Living) | London/SF/Dubai; 17 SaaS tools; Conduit since Dec 2023 | Conversational AI, unified inbox, call summaries, tagging | Title 70% guest support; header also 90% of guest communication; CEO calls 70% “very realistic”; 80–90% also described as a goal |

Haven: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026). Cascadia: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cascadia-getaways). HomeHop: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/homehop). Canbnb: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb). Bocobay: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bocobay). Cosmica: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/cosmica). Bali/Easy BnB: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays). The Flex: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex).

Recurring STR situations: listing growth that used to require headcount, prior AI or Intercom misfit, split inboxes, overnight coverage, and acquisition or exit math. Canbnb’s body also calls the onboarding product “HostAI,” which is not resolved on the page. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/canbnb)

### Hotel and hotel-like proof

| Customer | Situation | Named use | Reported result |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Lauderdale Boutique Hotel | Owner-operator; Jurny then other call services ($4k→$1.2k/mo, slow replies); Conduit since Dec 2024 | “AI-powered support platform and 24/7 staffed support team” replacing a call center | Support $4,000→$600/mo; response 57 min→2 min avg; NOI +≥$3,400/mo; >$500k modeled asset value at 8% cap |
| Wynwood House | Hospitality + real estate in 7 countries; using since Oct 2025; Guesty + ChatGPT + translation + Sheets | Unified inbox, AI replies/translation, sentiment, shift-handoff summaries | Resolution 14–15 min → 3 min; 4.8 Airbnb rating in Colombia (not claimed as a lift) |

Lauderdale: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/lauderdale-hotel). Wynwood: [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/wynwood-house). Lauderdale is the only named **hotel** P&L story here. Wynwood is multi-market CX, not hotel-group operations. Index titles for BlueGems, Moxxi, Renjoy/Joy, and an unnamed 35-property 96% automation story have no bodies in this pack, so those figures are unused. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers)

## What the results do and do not establish

They establish, as **company-attributed** stories: high STR automation after knowledge-base and workflow work (Haven was already installed at ~40%); some operators reporting stable communication scores while automating (Haven 4.8–4.9, Cascadia locked at 4.9); a boutique hotel owner reporting lower support cost, faster replies, fewer refunds, and a cap-rate translation of NOI; multi-market tool consolidation (Wynwood, Cosmica); a named Intercom move (Bocobay); recovery from a failed AI vendor (HomeHop); and an exit/labor story that replaced eleven VAs (Bali/Easy BnB)—unlike Haven, which says nobody was laid off because of AI. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/bali-luxury-stays)

They do **not** establish a typical rate, a price, or that [Guest Portals](#knowledge/product-portals) or Operations (nav: coming soon) produced these outcomes. Lauderdale’s $500k is the owner’s 8% cap-rate model, not an appraisal or closed sale. The Flex header “17 tools replaced by Conduit” and “90% of guest communication automated” sit beside a 70% title, a 70% CEO quote, and 80–90% as a future build. Haven’s Guest Favorite share is 59% in the header and 55% in the TL;DR; About says 230+ properties vs ~270 in the body. Bocobay’s 80% / hundreds of hours are not derived in the article. Site widget “4.7 / 5” on G2 is not a named-customer result. [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/the-flex) [Source](https://www.conduit.ai/customers/haven-2026)

## Matching proof to a campaign

Use **one named story per motion**. Keep customer, time window, and caveat in the same sentence as the number. Do not average rates across accounts.

| Prospect situation | Best-fit named proof | Do not stretch to |
|---|---|---|
| STR scale without linear guest-support hiring | Haven; HomeHop; Canbnb 60% of ~1,500 msgs/week | Hotel groups or a guaranteed 90% |
| Absorb an acquisition without a new call center | Cascadia first PM company | “All integrations complete in a week” |
| NOI, OM, or exit multiple | Lauderdale $3.4k/mo NOI and 8% cap math; Bali ~$22k/mo and 75 units | Treat cap-rate as appraised or sold value |
| Leave Intercom / unify WhatsApp + OTA + phone | Bocobay | The 80% header stat without methodology |
| Multi-country, multilingual CX | Wynwood 7 countries, 15→3 min; Cosmica Italy/Dubai | Causing Wynwood’s 4.8 Colombia rating |
| After-hours voice | HomeHop 1–7 AM; Haven snowstorm (three human issues) | 24/7 autopilot as current state |
| Stop building messaging AI in-house | Bali halted internal tool; Flex left comms out of a homegrown PMS | Conduit replacing the customer’s PMS |

See [ICP · vacation-rental operators](#knowledge/icp-rentals), [ICP · hotel operators](#knowledge/icp-hotels), [Product catalog & capability map](#knowledge/products-capabilities), and [Qualification & account research playbook](#knowledge/buying-triggers).

## Evidence gaps

Hotel-group and independent-hotel proof beyond Lauderdale is missing from this pack. No story isolates Portals, a standalone price, or a contract start vs. result window. Index-only stories (BlueGems, 96% at 35 properties, Moxxi, Renjoy) are unusable until bodies exist. Staffing outcomes conflict in kind (Haven: no AI layoffs; Bali: eleven VAs replaced). Automation denominators (messages vs support vs guest communication) are not defined consistently. Cascadia’s March vs December, HomeHop’s June 2025 vs “two years,” and Bali’s founded-2025 vs using-since-December-2024 need reconciliation before legal or investor use.
open_questions: What methodology sits behind Bocobay’s 80% resolution rate and “100s” of hours saved?
Which surfaces (Agents, Inbox, Workflows, voice, 24/7 staffed support) were in production for each named metric?
How should Cascadia’s March deploy vs December 2024 “using since,” HomeHop’s June 2025 vs “approximately two years,” and Bali founded-2025 vs using-since-December-2024 be reconciled?
Do index-only stories (BlueGems, 35-property 96% automation, Moxxi, Renjoy/Joy) have measurable bodies?
Is Lauderdale’s $500k an OM illustration, a completed sale, or only an 8% cap-rate model?

evidence_notes.quote: Haven went from needing around 25 support staff to running with two people per shift.

evidence_notes.statement: Lauderdale case study reports support cost falling from $4,000 to $600 per month.
Lauderdale owner models $3,400 monthly NOI gain as over $500,000 asset value at an 8% cap rate.
evidence_notes.quote: At an 8% Cap Rate, that $3,400 monthly gain translates into over $500,000 in added asset value.

evidence_notes.statement: Cascadia write-up reports 60% automation and 4.9 communication scores across 100 properties.
evidence_notes.quote: Within months, the company reached 60 percent automation  and 4.9 communication scores across across 100 properties.

evidence_notes.quote: When Mayra joined Wynwood House, guests were waiting an average of 14–15 minutes for issue resolution.

evidence_notes.quote: HomeHop nearly tripled its portfolio in two years, from roughly 40 short-term rental listings to 108 across the Cleveland and Akron markets.

use_when: Selecting a named case study for ABM, outbound, or a deck
Reviewing a customer metric before it is reused in copy
Matching a prospect’s operating situation to public proof
decisions_supported: Which single named story to cite for a campaign
Whether a printed number is usable only with its caveat
Whether hotel versus STR proof in this pack is sufficient for an account
do_not_infer: That the 300+ brand count or a logo wall means those accounts run a given product
That any one automation or savings rate is typical or guaranteed
That Portals or Operations drove these outcomes
That staffing stories always mean layoffs or never mean layoffs

evidence_validation: Exact passages checked; interpretation and proposed policies require review.
